resources.string: The choice applies to the whole app right away.
Road data: this app does not show a map. It loads road data for the speed limit and street names.
When you are too fast, the HUD shows speed and speed limit in bold. Off: never warns.
Warns from this many km/h over the limit (0 to 30).

Beep-beep-beep, once per speeding event and only again after you have dropped below the limit. The sound comes from the phone (e.g. to your intercom), music gets quieter briefly. Only with a connected HUD and only for a limit from the map data, not for an estimated one.

A single tone before something comes up ahead. Sound only, nothing on the HUD. Level crossings, pedestrian crossings and traffic calming need imported road data (card \"Import road data\"); tiles loaded online do not know these points. The bend warning works with both.
Tone before a level crossing ahead. You do not always have to stop, it is only a hint. The tone comes a little later than for a pedestrian crossing.
Tone before a pedestrian crossing ahead, early enough that you could stop calmly (the faster you are, the earlier).
Tone before speed bumps, humps, narrowings and other traffic calming ahead.

Tone before a very sharp bend ahead when you are clearly too fast for it (at least 10 km/h over the bend speed that follows from the radius of the bend). It comes early enough to brake comfortably, once per bend. Not in towns, not in residential and access roads, not below about 40 km/h. It is based on the road shape in the map data: where that is drawn roughly, a bend can look sharper than it is.
Low: only the tightest hairpins. Normal: sharp bends too. High: already at medium bends if you are fast.
Use additional hints from the map
Speed zones (for example \"Zone 30\") and source tags such as \"in town\" or \"outside town\" from the map data. These are real map data and they can also trigger the speed warning.
When the map data has no limit
Germany only. If the map data has no limit, 50 (residential or lit road) or 100 (country road) is assumed. Motorways get no assumption. Estimated limits never trigger a speed warning.
Passing a town sign (entrance) gives \"in town\", passing the exit sign gives \"outside town\". Applies until the next sign, at most 2.5 km.
If the section before or after on the same road has a limit, it is taken over.
Read a map file (.osm.pbf) or load it directly from the internet. Afterwards the app also works without network. Several regions one after another are possible.
On: the app loads nothing from the internet any more (no regions either) and uses only the stored and imported roads. Off: missing areas are loaded online as before.

Warns about fixed speed cameras ahead on your road, with a message on the HUD and, if \"Sound for cameras\" is on, with a sound. The data comes from OpenStreetMap and from your own camera list (see below). OpenStreetMap has gaps: mobile cameras and section controls are missing. In Germany and some other countries such a warning is not allowed for drivers.
Short, Normal or Long. The faster you drive, the earlier the warning comes: at 100 km/h about 280 m before the camera, at 50 km/h about 140 m.
Beep-beep-beep, once per camera, as soon as the warning comes. Independent of the sound when speeding. The sound comes from the phone, music gets quieter briefly. Only with a connected HUD.
Own camera list, for example from SCDB. Choose the GPX files, several at once are possible. The data stays on your phone only. A new selection replaces the old list.
Cameras at traffic lights (red light, often with speed check). Off: no warning for them.
Section controls (measurement over a stretch). Off: no warning for them.
Cameras in tunnels. Off: no warning for them.
This is the most space the app may use for saved road data. When it is full, the oldest data is deleted.
Both are needed for running with the display off and for reading OSMAnd.

For reading OSMAnd, calls and messages. The switch shows the real state. Tapping opens the Android settings, where you allow or revoke access. If the switch is greyed out there: App info, ⋮ top right, \"Allow restricted settings\".
So the service keeps running with the display off. The switch shows the real state. Tapping opens the matching Android page.

For trying the app in a car without a HUD: the app polls the GPS every second and plays all enabled warning tones (speed, cameras, hints, bends). Uses more battery, best switched on only for test drives.
Outside the season the app rests completely.
Normally the phone GPS. OSMAnd (speed from the notification) only for testing with a simulation. If the OSMAnd value is missing, the app uses GPS.
In case an arrow or a distance stays stuck after a simulation. The service must be running.
Shows individual display codes on the HUD for 5 seconds so you can see what your screen can do.
Off: repetitions are combined (for example 48 connection attempts in one line). On: every line separately, for troubleshooting. The file holds about 5 MB.
Only the Bluetooth connection to the HUD. Off: GPS, speed limit, street name and the tones keep running, just without the HUD. If the app does not find the wanted HUD for 10 minutes, it quits.
Off: the app rests completely (no Bluetooth, no GPS, no loading), the HUD is free for the Tilsberk app.
Riding without navigation: only OSMAnd is disconnected. GPS, speed limit and street name keep running. Calls, WhatsApp and Spotify too. Only works while \"App active\" is on.
Display mode of the HUD. The choice applies immediately, is saved and set again on the next connection. The preview shows which elements the mode uses.
Speed, speed limit, arrow, distance, remaining distance, remaining time, lane assist and clock.
Reduced: arrow, distance, speed limit, remaining distance, remaining time and clock. Without speed and lanes.
Compass, speed, speed limit, arrow, distance, remaining distance and arrival time. Shows calls and messages.
Speed, speed limit, arrow, distance, remaining distance, remaining time and street name (next street, otherwise current). Shows calls and messages.
Arrow with distance and two freely selectable lines.
Four freely selectable lines, for example speed, limit, ride time and distance.
How far before the turn the arrow, distance and lane hint appear. Earlier on fast roads.
The arrow appears at a distance of:
The arrow is always visible, no matter how far away the turn still is.
While navigation is running, the HUD shows a straight-ahead arrow until the next turn is close enough. If OSMAnd stops reporting or the destination is reached, it disappears.
Shows calls and WhatsApp messages on the HUD, only in Explorer and City. Needs notification access. The battery warning exists only in Guide, Cruiser and Explorer.
Calls stay on the HUD as long as it rings.
Messages appear for 5 seconds as a call symbol.

When a new track starts, the HUD message field (where calls also appear) shows the artist for 4 s, then a 1 s pause, then the title for 4 s (at most 19 characters each). Other music apps too. Only in Explorer and City; calls and messages take priority.

Shows a warning symbol on the HUD when the phone battery falls below the limit. Only in Guide, Cruiser and Explorer, not in the other displays. It disappears again when the battery is 5 % above the limit or the phone is charging.
The HUD controls the brightness itself. Off: you set a fixed level. Applies immediately and is set again on connecting.
Shows the adjustment image on the HUD to align the device on the helmet. Only with a connected HUD. When switched off, the HUD returns to the selected display mode.
The recording only ends when you stop it. If the motorcycle stands for 3 minutes, it pauses automatically and continues when you ride off. Saved as GPX in Download/GPX-Tracking.
Always included: track, time and speed. Additionally (off until you switch it on; cannot be changed during a recording):

The barometer measures altitude, the GPS gives the base level. The lean angle is only an estimate from the gyro sensor and GPS speed (from about 15 km/h) and is most accurate when the phone sits firmly. A CSV table for Excel is added to every ride.

The overview is calculated from your saved rides. Violations are only counted for rides where speed limits were known (extra recording: speed limit). The season follows Tools → Season; without a season the calendar year counts.
Tap or swipe over a chart to show the value (blue). The marker moves along in all charts and on the map. The map images come from OpenStreetMap and need internet when first opened.

OSMAnd HUD Bridge is an unofficial hobby project. It has no connection to Tilsberk, Digades or OSMAnd. All names and trademarks mentioned belong to their owners. \"Tilsberk\" and \"DVision\" are only mentioned to describe which device the app works with. The preview images and the app icon are my own drawings.

No warranty. The display can fail or be wrong (arrows, distances, speed limits, street names). Do not rely on it while riding. Traffic signs and traffic rules always take precedence. Use at your own risk, without any liability.

• The app reads notifications from OSMAnd, WhatsApp and calls, solely to show them on the HUD. Nothing is passed on.\n• Without imported data, the approximate position is sent to an Overpass server (OpenStreetMap) for street names and speed limits. With the \"Offline data\" switch (Speed limit tab) nothing is sent.\n• The log is stored on the device only. It can contain names of callers or senders. Check it before you share it.
